title: Release Corridor UX — Guided Split Tuning & Immediate Undo Microflow
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design a compact, low-friction rollout surface ("Release Corridor") for the Redwood Console that enables engineers and PMs to tune traffic splits, preview downstream impact, and perform an immediate, one-click undo. The Corridor is intended for short-run canaries and A/B experiments where quick adjustments and fast recoveries matter. Scope includes: compact controls (slider + numeric input + presets), live preview of percent allocations across variants, simulated request path visualizer, a safety gate checklist, and an immutable snapshot used for instant rollback. Work covers high-fidelity prototypes, accessibility review, engineering handoff notes, and usability testing with two internal platform teams.
acceptance_criteria: Prototype demonstrates slide-to-adjust traffic with live preview updating expected per-variant token distribution
Safety checklist prevents expansion beyond preset release windows unless acknowledged
Undo button reverts traffic back to the previous snapshot within 2s in prototype simulation
Design tokens follow Console theming and meet AA contrast on primary controls
Handoff document contains interaction spec, animation timing, and ARIA semantics for assistive tech

design_assets: Figma frame: Corridor / Main - Slider + Numeric Input
Figma frame: Corridor / Safety Checklist Modal
decisions: Compact ribbon pattern chosen over full-page editor to reduce context switches.
Undo is modeled as a rollback snapshot event (auditable) rather than a local undo stack to ensure consistency across Dedicated/Private deployments.
Simulation pane will use sampled telemetry heuristics instead of live traffic to avoid perf impact on production.
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls + ARIA live regions for preview updates required.
